sections.html:
Columbus and Muscogee County have shared one government since the start of 1971, so Columbus is both the only city and the county seat. There is no separate city tax bill to track. The county hugs the Alabama border along the Chattahoochee, and Fort Benning takes up roughly a quarter of the land.

The July 2025 estimate is 202,171 people, down 2.3% from the 206,922 counted in 2020. Owners live in 50.8% of homes, which leaves about half of the housing to renters, so many buyers here are investors as well as owner-occupants. Expect those buyers to ask for the tax history on the parcel early in negotiations.

Three separate bodies touch a Muscogee County bill: one mails and collects it, one sets the value and rules on exemptions, and one hears disputes.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills, takes payments, tracks delinquent accounts and posts tax sale lists at columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner
  • Board of Tax Assessors: fair market value, exemption approvals and the yearly assessment notice
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury, it rules on disputes over value, a denied homestead, freeport and taxability

The assessors meet Wednesday mornings at 9:00 in the City Services Building, 3111 Citizens Way. Call the Tax Commissioner for counter hours and a written payoff figure before you list the house. The commissioner's site also has a parcel search, homestead forms, a delinquent tax section and a tax sale registration class.

Bills for real and personal property reach owners in late summer. Payment comes in two steps: 40% or the full amount in October, then the remaining 60% in December. Follow the dates printed on your own bill, because month details can shift from year to year.

  • April 1: mobile home bills come due, the current-year homestead window closes, and returns on business equipment, aircraft and watercraft are due at the assessor
  • May: assessment notices go out, and the appeal period begins
  • July: millage rates are set after advertised public input
  • August: bills are mailed
  • October: first payment, 40% or everything
  • December: the remaining 60%

Payment can be made online with the parcel number from the bill. Splitting the bill into two payments helps cash flow, but if you are selling, the closing attorney will usually ask for the whole year's balance at once so the lien question never comes up.

sections.h2: How can an owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal within 45 days after the date printed on the assessment notice. Notices go out in May, so the clock runs through early summer. A homestead application filed in that stretch can stand in for an appeal.

Put your reasons plainly in the letter, such as value, taxability, uniformity or a refused exemption, and keep a copy. The Board of Equalization decides the matter. Ask the assessors whether another route applies to your parcel type, and call before the 45 days run out rather than after.

Overpayment has its own path. A taxpayer can request a refund in writing for tax assessed in error, with the claim starting inside three years of payment.

The basic exemption takes $2,000 off the state portion and $13,500 off the local assessed value for an owner who lives in the house. It freezes the assessment but skips the slice of millage used to retire bonds.

  • Elderly school-tax exemption: owner 62 or older, net income at or under $10,000 the prior year, school tax only
  • Elderly general exemption: owner 65 or older with the same $10,000 test, up to $4,000 off the state portion and $21,500 off local value
  • Floating exemption: 62 or older, household gross income $30,000 or less, covers state and county tax but not schools
  • Disabled veteran: up to $117,014 off both the state portion and the local assessed value, with proof from the VA

The floating exemption replaces any other state and county exemption and may raise the first year's tax, so ask the assessors before choosing it. A buyer should confirm whether a new application is needed after closing.

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's whole bill in the eyes of the law. The Tax Commissioner does not divide it between buyer and seller. The closing paperwork does that.

If nobody pays, a lien goes under the January 1 owner's name. A seller can shift it to the buyer by delivering evidence within 90 days of the due date: a recorded deed in the buyer's name and wording in the closing papers that hands the tax to the buyer. The Tax Commissioner's buying and selling page walks through the process.

The office never sells tax liens or lien certificates. A parcel that finds no bidder at a tax sale rejoins the queue for later sales. Staff cannot offer legal advice, so see an attorney if a lien is already recorded.

Start with the parcel number on your bill. Use it on the commissioner's site to see the balance, and ask for a written payoff figure. Then check with the assessors that your exemption is on the account and that the assessment notice from May was not left unanswered.

If taxes are past due, ask the commissioner where the parcel stands on the delinquent list before an offer comes in, because a buyer's title search will find it. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender's tax review, and the unpaid amount is taken out of your proceeds at the table.

What to bring if you visit an office: the parcel number, a photo ID, the deed or closing statement if ownership just changed, and income records if you are applying for an elderly or floating exemption. For a written appeal, a copy of the assessment notice and any comparable sales or appraisal make the letter stronger. Keep proof of every payment, since a dispute over a missed installment is easier to settle with a receipt.

Fort Benning families should know that children there are zoned to Department of Defense schools for grades K-8, then attend county high schools. The Muscogee County School District serves every other address from kindergarten through grade 12.

faqs.q: If I close in the middle of a year, who is billed for that year?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 is liable for the full year. The closing documents split it between buyer and seller, and a lien can move to the buyer if proof arrives within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: Where do I find a parcel record or balance?
faqs.a: Use the search and pay links on columbusga.gov/taxcommissioner and enter the parcel number printed on your bill. Assessor records are on the city-county public access site.

faqs.q: Does a homestead filing replace an appeal?
faqs.a: Yes, during the 45-day period after the assessment notice a homestead application can be made in place of an appeal. For the current year, the general homestead cutoff is April 1.

faqs.q: Will the Tax Commissioner sell my lien to an investor?
faqs.a: No. The office does not sell tax liens or lien certificates. An unsold property returns to the rotation for future tax sales.

faqs.q: Which public schools cover Muscogee County addresses?
faqs.a: The Muscogee County School District serves everything except Fort Benning for kindergarten through grade 12. Fort Benning children are zoned to Department of Defense schools for grades K-8, then attend county high schools.
